issues.label: Agent-native semantic GPU debugger and profiler
Deterministic CPU semantic simulator and virtual GPU runtime

capabilities.label: Rust ownership and result flow
capabilities.detail: rustc remains the only Rust borrow checker: it enforces moves, borrows, lifetimes, visibility, and local typestate. Fe2O3 extends those rules with sealed non-Clone GPU capabilities and workload-neutral cross-invocation verification. Typed kernels may return KernelResult and use ?, while the macro emits a private unit-ABI entry wrapper and the compiler retains the helper's real MIR. Err ends only the current invocation and is not a host-visible error channel.

capabilities.label: Pliron context ownership
capabilities.detail: Process-local context identities, registered dialects, and context-bound handles are checked before operations are inspected. Generic safety passes execute today; issue #140 tracks stronger owner-aware upstream arena handles rather than blocking the production verifier sequence.

capabilities.label: Generic pre-lowering safety
capabilities.detail: The fixed nine-pass workload-neutral pre-lowering sequence verifies rooted tensor-layout composition, ranked bounds and checked machine-index arithmetic, atomic legality, cross-invocation race freedom, complete hierarchy ownership, barrier and SIMT collective protocol convergence, staged pipeline lifecycles and epoch-slot relations, workgroup-memory initialization/publication, and semantic refinement. The semantic stage now fails closed on unproved loop progress and on changed numerical operator trees without an error theorem. A separate compiler-supplied target precondition checks launch geometry, static LDS use, and origin-bound host allocation size and alignment before the same nine passes; it grants no launch authority. Compiler-derived tensor roots connect producers to operand and accumulator consumers; incompatible ABI flow and producer joins are compile-time errors. Every diagnostic includes a concrete repair or states the missing proof obligation. Rejected and Incomplete findings both stop production compilation before lowering.

capabilities.label: Middle-end evidence custody
capabilities.detail: The production middle end has one fixed nine-pass sequence and one live evidence producer: ProductionMiddleEndEvidenceV5. The pipeline-protocol pass runs after barrier convergence and before workgroup-memory verification, so its epoch certificate becomes an input to must-initialization/publication checking. The V4 decoder is strict and archival-only; it cannot produce live evidence or grant refinement, lowering, artifact, or launch authority. The caller-declared ProductionReferenceProofV1 and RequireReferenceEquivalent API is removed. Target-aware entry points perform bounded structural inventory before recursive PLIRON verification and launch-contract scanning, with malformed, nested, unsupported, or over-limit input failing as FE2O3-TARGET-000. Authenticated production projection now carries checked tiled and row-striped indices, success paths, physical extents, dominance, and provenance into live race analysis and retained KIR lowering for the supported dynamic fragment.

capabilities.label: Unified production route
capabilities.detail: Ordinary safe Rust enters one compiler architecture: semantic MIR is projected into ranked PLIRON, checked normalization and the fixed verification sequence run there, and the admitted result is carried into target-selected canonical Kernel IR, formal-memory admission, and target LLVM. The retired standalone AMDGCN/PLIRON-to-LLVM and KIR/PLIRON bridge packages have been deleted. At commit 1dd61a01, the generic gfx942 path compiled the displayed dynamic GEMM and attention sources through HSACO and the qualification runner executed both on MI300X against safe Rust oracles. The feature-gated qualification launch does not grant protected Worker V3 publication or general source-to-machine refinement. GFX950 Semantic MIR V6 and Kernel IR V9 selection is derived from live collective and LDS-transpose operations rather than a workload or function name; under the exact full-active Wave64 profile, FP32 reductions accept each nonzero power-of-two tile width through 64. Unsupported widths, targets, profiles, and dynamic source lanes fail closed. Unsupported effects, witnesses, and ownership forms remain deliberately fail-closed.

capabilities.label: Bounded compiler analysis
capabilities.detail: The sole fixed nine-stage analysis route shares closed CFG, SSA, uniformity, sparse index, Presburger, provenance, memory-order, SIMT, pipeline-epoch, and bounded invocation facts without recognizing a workload. The pipeline stage proves stage, commit, wait, consume-or-discard, and release order; release-before-reuse; epoch modulo buffer count; disjoint storage; uniform dynamic bounds; and summarized prologue, steady-state, and drain regions without unrolling runtime loops. Analysis-only stages are protected by a context-wide monotonic PLIRON mutation-attempt epoch, exact structural checkpoints, and sealed report custody. Independent raw replay remains Complete only for the admitted static bounded-access fragment, and nonempty tensor-layout replay remains Incomplete until external roots have explicit operational-SSA provenance. Natural-loop and dominator inventories are built once, and epoch-aware summaries handle nested dynamic loops and multiple loop-carried block arguments under explicit resource budgets. Checked tiled and row-striped recipes carry an exact index, checked-success capability, destination physical extent, source provenance, and launch coordinates; live validation proves supported active store maps injective across workgroups, lanes, and components. Generic explicit affine and bounded Presburger maps remain supported. One production transformation folds exact preceding index constants after independent exact typed replay and private receipt custody. Unknown aliases, unsupported maps, divergent collective bounds, malformed pipelines, missing drains, wrong slots or epochs, and noncanonical or wrapping progress obligations fail closed. The analyses and lowering contain no GEMM, attention, routing, or other workload selector.

capabilities.label: Safe Rust functional references
capabilities.detail: The published compiler baseline runs one generated Verus checker that replays supported exact pointwise integer and compiler-side IEEE operator-DAG formulas from compiler-derived coordinates, domains, preconditions, and values; no generic relation premise supplies equality. PLIRON separately proves and reconciles total coverage, allocation separation, frames, schedules, and ordered-product identity, while a private move-only join requires both structural and formula reports. Status-Checked policy staging grants no authority. Canonical positive-step loops carry termination evidence only when the backedge update is statically nonwrapping; concrete nontermination is Rejected and an unsupported ranking proof is Incomplete. Dynamic slice reads are complete only for exact identical symbolic ranked extents or overflow-checked bounded static affine intervals; unrelated independent lengths, missing assertions, unsafe intervals, and overflow fail closed. Identical live typed floating-point trees receive an exact-zero error certificate; reassociation, changed operation order, and nonzero ErrorBounded replay remain unsupported. A tensor reference must name the exact propagated accumulator result root and match its component count and semantic scalar before value/store refinement can pass. This composes the target-owned physical layout proof with the safe Rust/Verus semantic obligation; the reference is not treated as a hardware-layout oracle. Maintainers report that, on mi300x, the listed functional-refinement and Verus publication commands passed against this compiler revision using the pinned Verus executable. The website retains no immutable command transcript or run record for that qualification, so it is not independently verifiable publication evidence. Even if reproduced, it is compiler and host-proof validation only; it grants no target, artifact, launch, hardware, performance, or universal-correctness authority. Compiler extraction/projection and analysis-result or transformation soundness, target IEEE values, LLVM-or-later lowering, target instruction arithmetic, artifacts, launch, hardware, and performance remain outside the claim.

capabilities.label: Target finalization
capabilities.detail: At commit 1dd61a01, the displayed dynamic GEMM and attention sources emitted gfx942 LLVM and HSACO, launched through the feature-gated qualification runtime on MI300X, and matched independent safe Rust CPU references. The generated code objects were inspected for MFMA, barriers, LDS traffic, workgroup geometry, kernarg size, and 2,048-byte static LDS. Protected Worker V3 publication, durable artifact currentness, general compiler refinement, and universal numerical correctness remain separate.

capabilities.label: Runtime and persistent execution
capabilities.detail: At the published baseline, generated #[kernel(typed)] bindings use the direct-KFD GeneratedKfdReadSlice, GeneratedKfdWriteSlice, and GeneratedKfdReadWriteSlice capabilities over retained host borrows. The default fe2o3-host dependency closure contains fe2o3-kfd, fe2o3-runtime, and fe2o3-runtime-protocol while excluding fe2o3-core, fe2o3-hip-sys, fe2o3-hsa-runtime, and Worker V2. The deprecated HIP-buffer and HSA-lifecycle host surface is qualification-only behind the explicit qualification-legacy-hip-hsa feature; fe2o3-hsa-runtime opts into that feature for its reviewed adapter. Separately, fe2o3-runtime exposes a typed RuntimeContextV1 with context-local devices, streams, allocations, modules, kernels, events, asynchronous submissions, and sealed backend handles. Its bounded RuntimeWorkerBackendV1 transport checks protocol compatibility but does not authenticate the worker, artifact, or host, and no standalone KFD or HSA worker executable is shipped. The direct-KFD adapter admits one gfx942 device and serializes logical streams over one native queue. Neither backend advertises peer copy, multi-device operation, atomics, or collectives. The Worker V3 direct-KFD preparation boundary exists, but no reviewed production verifier is wired and the application examples remain fail closed. These records establish no general HIP/HSA parity, protected production launch, multi-GPU, collective, performance, source-level hardware debugging, or profiling authority.

capabilities.label: Compiler execution attestation
capabilities.detail: The protected authority service admits a hardened static issuer and immutable Ed25519 key, then maintains one signed, singleton, crash-safe compiler-execution journal with exact recovery and mutation checks. No public API can construct the supervised compiler-occurrence token. Supervised occurrence production, the bounded service loop, Worker V3 receipt carriage, and its independent protected rollback ledger remain open, so this mechanism grants no compiler, publication, load, or launch authority.

capabilities.label: Semantic debugging and profiling
capabilities.detail: The CPU semantic debugger records bounded execution-derived checkpoints behind a strict versioned JSONL session. It supports work-item, logical Wave32/Wave64, workgroup, and dispatch views; KIR and compiler-bundle-bound source resolution; breakpoints and stepping; allocation-relative watchpoints and memory; SSA snapshots; captured stacks; faults; exact schedule replay; deterministic reverse navigation; and bounded diagnoses for retained out-of-bounds and barrier-divergence failures. Source Map V1 exposes source sites without variables. The opt-in V2 bundle binds only exact one-to-one, never-mutated kernel parameters to KIR values and returns distinct typed states for every other variable gap. Counter Capture V2 import/comparison, PC Sample Capture V3 import/paging/hotspots, and Semantic Profiler Bundle V4 dispatch, comparison, and next-capture queries are implemented for strict retained inputs; the website renders those retained projections. Compiler-bundle binding authenticates exact local map/KIR content, not protected compiler execution. Direct-KFD Live GPU V3 has observed a stopped MI300X queue envelope and control effects, but inner gfx942 wave, lane, register, PC, and target-memory records remain unavailable. The ROCgdb MI backend admits generic thread/control records but has not authenticated live GPU wave state. CPU logical waves are not hardware waves. A real application-dispatch rocprofv3-to-import round trip, supported ATT decode, full protected source/ISA qualification matrix, automated live diagnosis, and production hardware source/KIR control remain open in issue #215; none of the retained profiler fixtures grants GPU execution or performance authority.

capabilities.label: Source-to-bundle CPU semantic simulation
capabilities.detail: The Linux-only fe2o3-kir-sim CLI securely admits either exact verified canonical KIR V7 or an authority-free .fe2sim plus a strict typed request. fe2o3-export-sim supplies the bundle from ordinary attributed Rust through the sole production source/MIR/PLIRON/KIR transaction, with an embedded compiler-bundle-bound map; it is not a resurrected source-first simulator route. The simulator executes the supported reachable subset with bounded deterministic CPU semantics, formal memory, checked resident accounting, copied results, conflict observations, and an opt-in debugger sink. Canonical and seeded schedules persist exact artifact, request, target, limits, context, transcript, coverage, seed, and runnable decisions for strict replay, including debugger capture. Admitted integer atomic kinds and legal scopes/orderings, explicit fences, and exact software F16/BF16/F32/F64 scalar bits are implemented; unsupported math, float atomics, wave/matrix operations, and other absent semantics fail closed. The bundle authenticates local content, not compiler execution, and grants no source refinement, proof, race-freedom theorem, GPU equivalence, artifact/load/launch authority, timing, profiling, performance, or performance prediction. Issue #216 tracks remaining semantic and virtual-runtime breadth.
